pattern.top_pattern: NY acute hospital pressure is tied to digestive MCC and postpartum episodes
pattern.what_is_impacting: NY Commercial Local Group ACUTE HOSPITAL spend in PPO and EPO, with digestive MCC and postpartum drivers
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
pattern.pattern_details: NY inpatient pressure is showing up operationally in ACUTE HOSPITAL PPO and EPO, but the underlying cases are concentrated in digestive MCC and postpartum episodes. Rare digestive admissions account for a large share of the increase, while postpartum episodes are appearing in both the operational and clinical findings. This points to a focused inpatient management issue rather than a broad statewide reimbursement problem.
pattern.why_it_matters: NY combines real inpatient growth with concentrated clinical drivers, so broad policy changes would be less effective than targeted hospital and episode management.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Review NY ACUTE HOSPITAL authorization and concurrent review rules for digestive MCC and postpartum stays, and perform case-level review of the rare digestive admissions before any network or reimbursement changes.
pattern.validation_reason: A large share of the increase comes from low-volume, high-cost digestive cases, so case-level confirmation is needed before scaling business action.
evidence_summary: NY PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL added about $0.6M, led by Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC (+$0.4M) and postpartum/postabortion diagnoses (+$0.2M).
Rare NY digestive cases added about $1.5M, including ulcer of intestine (+$0.5M across 3 admissions) and exomphalos (+$0.4M across 3 admissions).
Smaller NY EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL pockets added about $0.1M across postpartum and kidney/urinary cases.
